edges.description: Covalent adduction is one of several cooperating consequences of radical formation that together kill the hepatocyte; the cited review is explicit that no single one of them is the sole cause, which is why the edge is typed as having known omitted intermediates rather than DIRECT.
intermediate_mechanisms: Lipid peroxidation of membrane polyunsaturated fatty acids
Loss of cellular calcium sequestration and homeostasis
Reactive aldehyde (4-hydroxynonenal) adduction of functional proteins
edges.source: Reactive Metabolite Formation and Covalent Protein Adduction

edges.description: Dying and stressed hepatocytes are the trigger for the liver's resident-macrophage response; this edge carries that initiating step, separate from the mediator-release event it leads to.

edges.source: IL-11 Signalling in Hepatic Stellate Cells

edges.description: Activated stellate-cell-derived myofibroblasts are the effector cells that synthesize and deposit the excessive extracellular matrix; this edge is the step by which the central fibrogenic event proceeds into matrix accumulation.
Persistent excessive matrix deposition and scar remodeling distort the normal hepatic architecture, the transition from fibrosis to the architectural end stage of cirrhosis.

Distorted lobular architecture and nodular regeneration are the structural component of the rise in intrahepatic vascular resistance; the portal_hypertension module's own trigger-node description names "fibrosis and architectural distortion" as this structural arm.
Loss of functional hepatocyte mass to fibrous replacement and nodular remodeling impairs the liver's synthetic capacity, producing decompensated synthetic dysfunction.
Advanced architectural distortion is part of the acute-decompensation picture in which jaundice is a defining clinical complication.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of functional hepatocyte mass and impaired bilirubin conjugation/excretion

edges.description: A rise in the resistance of the hepatic vascular bed raises the pressure required to drive portal blood through it, matching the module's own trigger-to-central-effector edge.

TGF-beta is a dominant inducer of autocrine IL-11 in fibroblasts, placing IL-11 receptor signalling downstream of TGF-beta; the hepatic stellate cell arm is evidenced on the target node (PMID:31078624).
edges.target: IL-11 Signalling in Hepatic Stellate Cells

edges.description: Increased splanchnic inflow into a high-resistance hepatic bed raises portal pressure further.
The portosystemic pressure gradient from portal hypertension opens and dilates submucosal collateral vessels in the esophagus.
intermediate_mechanisms: Portosystemic collateral formation and dilation of pre-existing gastro-oesophageal venous channels

edges.description: Raised sinusoidal and portal pressure drives interstitial filtration and fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity.
Portal hypertension drives portosystemic collateral shunting, by which ammonia and other gut-derived neurotoxins bypass hepatic clearance and reach the systemic circulation.
intermediate_mechanisms: Portosystemic shunting permitting gut-derived neurotoxins to bypass the liver

edges.description: Passive splenic congestion from the elevated portal pressure enlarges the spleen.
Reduced hepatic synthesis of clotting factors produces the abnormal coagulation cascade.
Rupture of a dilated, high-pressure submucosal esophageal varix bleeds directly into the gastrointestinal lumen.
Sustained heavy drinking produces hepatocyte apoptosis, the initiating injury from which the fibrogenic cascade proceeds.

Administration of carbon tetrachloride is the route by which the hepatic adduct burden is established: the covalent binding measured on the target node only occurs where CCl4 is supplied to a cytochrome P-450-competent liver, and it scales with the amount of that enzyme available to activate it. Britton et al. report the in vivo counterpart directly, with chlordecone raising hepatic cytochrome P-450 by 67% and increasing covalent binding of labelled CCl4 metabolites to microsomal protein and lipid in the intact rat; that sentence carries a bracketed isotope label the snippet validator strips, so the dose-response sentence from the same abstract is quoted below instead.
edges.target: Reactive Metabolite Formation and Covalent Protein Adduction

edges.description: TGF-beta 1 drives the hTERT-HSC compartment through the defining transition of this node, inducing the myofibroblast marker program and the matrix products that follow from it.
edges.limitations: The stellate compartment is an hTERT-immortalized line rather than primary quiescent stellate cells, and activation is driven by exogenous TGF-beta 1 rather than by signals arising from the injured hepatocyte compartment. The abstract reports marker expression and secreted matrix proteins, not deposited fibrillar collagen, matrix stiffening or stellate cell contraction.
edges.source: Akura Twin 384-well liver fibrosis microphysiological system (HepaRG/THP-1 and hTERT-HSC microtissues)

edges.description: A monocytic compartment co-cultured with the hepatocyte microtissues supplies the inflammatory arm of the fibrotic cascade and is activated alongside it.
edges.limitations: THP-1 is a circulating monocytic leukemia line, not a resident Kupffer cell, and the system has no sinusoidal endothelial or lymphocyte compartment. Activation is driven by exogenous TGF-beta 1, so the abstract does not establish that hepatocyte injury in the paired well is what activates these cells.
edges.source: Akura Twin 384-well liver fibrosis microphysiological system (HepaRG/THP-1 and hTERT-HSC microtissues)

edges.description: The same monocytic compartment's secreted PAI-1 is read as an output of the co-culture's mediator-release program, distinct from the marker induction that signals the compartment's own activation.
edges.limitations: The system has no sinusoidal endothelial or lymphocyte compartment, and activation is driven by exogenous TGF-beta 1, so the abstract does not establish that hepatocyte injury in the paired well is what drives this mediator release. PAI-1 is a fibrinolysis inhibitor rather than one of the cytokines (TGF-beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha) this node's description names, so it stands in for the mediator-release event rather than measuring it directly.
edges.source: Akura Twin 384-well liver fibrosis microphysiological system (HepaRG/THP-1 and hTERT-HSC microtissues)

edges.description: Hepatotoxicant and TGF-beta 1 challenge injures the HepaRG compartment, supplying the initiating injury this node describes.
edges.limitations: Injury is inferred from loss of albumin synthesis. The abstract reports no direct cell-death measurement - no caspase, LDH release or viability assay - so the death half of this node is not demonstrated.
edges.source: Akura Twin 384-well liver fibrosis microphysiological system (HepaRG/THP-1 and hTERT-HSC microtissues)

edges.description: TGF-beta 1 is applied exogenously as the driving stimulus of the model, so this node is manipulated rather than reproduced.
edges.limitations: Recombinant TGF-beta 1 is added directly to the medium in place of the endogenous, injury-driven, latent-TGF-beta activation route. The abstract reports downstream marker responses rather than SMAD2/3 phosphorylation, so the signalling step itself is not measured.
edges.source: Akura Twin 384-well liver fibrosis microphysiological system (HepaRG/THP-1 and hTERT-HSC microtissues)

nodes.description: High-throughput microphysiological system built on a 384-well microplate of 168 interconnected well pairs. HepaRG hepatocyte microtissues, with or without THP-1 monocytic cells, occupy the alpha well of each pair and hepatic stellate cell (hTERT-HSC) microtissues occupy the beta well, so hepatocellular injury and stellate activation are read out in separate but communicating compartments. A non-animal New Approach Methodology built to quantify the key events of the liver fibrosis Adverse Outcome Pathway under TGF-beta 1, methotrexate and acetaminophen challenge.
nodes.id: Akura Twin 384-well liver fibrosis microphysiological system (HepaRG/THP-1 and hTERT-HSC microtissues)

evidence.snippet: In a 3-year randomized clinical trial of 201 patients with portal hypertension, nonselective β-blockers (carvedilol or propranolol) reduced the risk of decompensation or death compared with placebo (16% vs 27%).

nodes.description: Carbon tetrachloride is the classical experimental hepatic fibrogen: a haloalkane bioactivated by hepatic cytochrome P-450 to a trichloromethyl radical that adducts hepatocellular macromolecules and, on repeated administration, drives the fibrogenic chain to cirrhosis. It is included here as the exposure that instantiates the chemically initiated arm of this entry's pathograph.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatotoxicity and mechanism of action of haloalkanes: carbon tetrachloride as a toxicological model.
evidence.snippet: Yet CCl4 continues to provide an important service today as a model substance to elucidate the mechanisms of action of hepatotoxic effects such as fatty degeneration, fibrosis, hepatocellular death, and carcinogenicity.

nodes.description: Bridging fibrous septa, regenerative nodules, and vascular remodeling distort the normal hepatic lobular architecture and impair hepatocyte function. This is the architectural end stage proper -- cirrhosis -- and is kept distinct from the upstream matrix-accumulation event ('Excessive Hepatic ECM Deposition'): fibrosis is the lesion, cirrhosis is the structural consequence of enough of it accumulating over enough time.

evidence.reference_title: Cellular mechanisms of tissue fibrosis. 1. Common and organ-specific mechanisms associated with tissue fibrosis.
evidence.snippet: Fibrosis is a pathological scarring process that leads to destruction of organ architecture and impairment of organ function.

evidence.reference_title: Management of coagulopathy in patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis.
evidence.snippet: Patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis have significantly impaired synthetic function. Many proteins involved in the coagulation process are synthesized in the liver. Routinely performed tests of the coagulation are abnormal in patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis.

nodes.description: Spironolactone and furosemide for ascites management.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Cirrhosis and Its Complications: A Review.
evidence.snippet: Compared with sequential initiation, combination aldosterone antagonist and loop diuretics were more likely to resolve ascites (76% vs 56%) with lower rates of hyperkalemia (4% vs 18%).

evidence.reference_title: AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Management of Ascites, Volume Overload, and Hyponatremia in Cirrhosis: Expert Review.
evidence.snippet: Patients with cirrhosis with ascites, hepatic hydrothorax, or volume overload should be managed with dietary sodium restriction and diuretics at the lowest effective dose, with dose escalation guided by symptoms, weight, urine output, and electrolyte/renal monitoring.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and therapeutic options for cirrhotic portal hypertension.

nodes.description: Activated hepatic stellate cells/myofibroblasts deposit excessive fibrillar collagen and other extracellular-matrix proteins in the hepatic parenchyma, disrupting sinusoidal exchange and forming the scar tissue that constitutes fibrosis -- the step between stellate-cell activation and the architectural distortion of cirrhosis proper. This is distinct from cirrhosis itself: fibrosis is matrix accumulation, cirrhosis is the architectural end stage downstream of it (see 'Cirrhotic Architectural Distortion').

nodes.description: Quiescent stellate cells transform into myofibroblasts, producing excessive collagen and extracellular matrix. This is the central event in liver fibrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Liver Fibrosis: From Basic Science towards Clinical Progress, Focusing on the Central Role of Hepatic Stellate Cells.
evidence.snippet: LF is a wound-healing process characterized by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins due to the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). In the healthy liver, quiescent HSCs metabolize and store retinoids. Upon fibrogenic activation, quiescent HSCs transdifferentiate into myofibroblasts; lose their vitamin A; upregulate α-smooth muscle actin; and produce proinflammatory soluble mediators, collagens, and inhibitors of ECM degradation. Activated HSCs are the main effector cells during hepatic fibrogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Liver Fibrosis: From Basic Science towards Clinical Progress, Focusing on the Central Role of Hepatic Stellate Cells.
evidence.snippet: In addition, the accumulation and activation of profibrogenic macrophages in response to hepatocyte death play a critical role in the initiation of HSC activation and survival.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic stellate cells as key target in liver fibrosis.
evidence.snippet: Transdifferentiation (or "activation") of hepatic stellate cells is the major cellular source of matrix protein-secreting myofibroblasts, the major driver of liver fibrogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic stellate cells as key target in liver fibrosis.
evidence.snippet: Paracrine signals from injured epithelial cells, fibrotic tissue microenvironment, immune and systemic metabolic dysregulation, enteric dysbiosis, and hepatitis viral products can directly or indirectly induce stellate cell activation.

nodes.description: Fibrogenic cytokine stimulation of hepatic stellate cells induces autocrine IL-11, which signals through IL11RA1 to activate ERK and drive the fibrotic stellate-cell programme. This IL-11 receptor-signalling arm is an organ-specific instance of the conserved IL-11 signalling module and feeds hepatic stellate cell activation; neutralizing anti-IL-11 (X203) or anti-IL11RA (X209) antibodies block it and reduce liver fibrosis.
nodes.id: IL-11 Signalling in Hepatic Stellate Cells

evidence.reference_title: Inhibiting Interleukin 11 Signaling Reduces Hepatocyte Death and Liver Fibrosis, Inflammation, and Steatosis in Mouse Models of Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis.
evidence.snippet: HSCs incubated with cytokines produced IL11, resulting in activation (phosphorylation) of ERK and expression of markers of fibrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Inhibiting Interleukin 11 Signaling Reduces Hepatocyte Death and Liver Fibrosis, Inflammation, and Steatosis in Mouse Models of Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis.
evidence.snippet: Neutralizing antibodies that block IL11 signaling reduce fibrosis, steatosis, hepatocyte death, inflammation and hyperglycemia in mice with diet-induced steatohepatitis.

evidence.reference_title: IL-11 is a crucial determinant of cardiovascular fibrosis.
evidence.snippet: IL-11 and its receptor (IL11RA) are expressed specifically in fibroblasts, in which they drive non-canonical, ERK-dependent autocrine signalling that is required for fibrogenic protein synthesis.

nodes.description: Fibrosis and architectural distortion, together with a dynamic vasoconstrictive phenotype acquired by sinusoidal cells, raise the resistance the hepatic vasculature offers to portal blood flow. This is the sinusoidal-resistance route the portal hypertension module documents for cirrhosis of any etiology, feeding the disorder-agnostic Portal Hypertension node below.

evidence.reference_title: The Molecular Mechanisms of Liver Fibrosis and Its Potential Therapy in Application.

evidence.snippet: Tofogliflozin prevented PH with attenuated intrahepatic vasoconstriction, sinusoidal capillarization, and remodeling independent of glycemic status in CCl4-treated rats.

nodes.description: Cytochrome P450-dependent bioactivation of a haloalkane hepatotoxicant generates a carbon-centred radical that binds covalently to hepatic macromolecules. For carbon tetrachloride the proximate species is the trichloromethyl radical, which trichloromethylates microsomal protein and lipid, preferentially in the centrilobular zone where oxygen tension is lowest and the glutathione-dependent protective route is least effective. The adduction is a measured quantity rather than an asserted step: covalent binding of 14C from labelled CCl4 is quantified against oxygen tension, added glutathione, cytochrome P-450 induction and CCl4 dose, and the protein-bound label localises to the cytochrome P-450 apoprotein mass range.
nodes.id: Reactive Metabolite Formation and Covalent Protein Adduction

evidence.reference_title: Hepatotoxicity and mechanism of action of haloalkanes: carbon tetrachloride as a toxicological model.
evidence.snippet: CCl4 is activated by cytochrome (CYP)2E1, CYP2B1 or CYP2B2, and possibly CYP3A, to form the trichloromethyl radical, CCl3*.

evidence.reference_title: Relationship of oxygen and glutathione in protection against carbon tetrachloride-induced hepatic microsomal lipid peroxidation and covalent binding in the rat. Rationale for the use of hyperbaric oxygen to treat carbon tetrachloride ingestion.
evidence.snippet: Lipid peroxidation and covalent binding of 14C fell progressively as O2 tension was increased from 1 to 21%. The addition of GSH decreased both lipid peroxidation and covalent binding

evidence.reference_title: Metabolic activation of carbon tetrachloride: induction of cytochrome P-450 with phenobarbital or 3-methylcholanthrene and its effect on covalent binding.
evidence.snippet: Most of protein-bound radioactivity is located in the mass range between 47 000 and 54 000 daltons, indicating that cytochrome P-450PB is the isoenzyme mainly responsible for CC14-activation

nodes.description: Arterial vasodilation in the splanchnic bed increases the volume of blood delivered into the portal system, while systemic vasodilation triggers compensatory cardiac output rise and sodium-retaining neurohormonal activation. This hyperdynamic circulatory syndrome aggravates, rather than compensates, the portal pressure raised by intrahepatic resistance, and is the arm nonselective beta-blockade acts on.
